"""Model layer: screenshot -> messages -> model call -> parsed action -> page pixels. Starts from the UI-TARS 1.5 reference implementation. What changed, in the order a step goes through it: 1. Screenshot size VLM_MAX_PIXELS / UITARSAgent.predict() Screenshots larger than 1440x810 are downscaled before sending. Otherwise the API downscales them itself, the model answers in the downscaled image's coordinates, and the reference code read those as page coordinates, so every click landed at 3/4 of its target. 2. Coordinate mapping parse_action_to_structure_output() The size of the image actually sent and the real viewport size are passed separately: page pixel = model coordinate x (viewport / sent). 3. Reply cleanup _truncate_to_first_action() / _SPECIAL_TOKEN Keep only the first Thought/Action pair (the model likes to invent the rest of the conversation, fake finished() included); strip self-generated chat-template tokens such as <|eot_id|>; drop trailing junk after the action (e.g. "
"). 4. Action feedback _obs_content() When the executor reports that the last action had no effect or was rejected, that note is sent to the model in front of the screenshot. 5. Model-call retries UITARSAgent.predict() Back off and retry on 403 / 429 / 5xx / timeouts; attempts and total time are set in config.json. A final failure returns ("client error", "FAIL") so the main loop ends the task quickly and still writes result.json. 6. Usage logging _log_usage(), off by default; for local diagnostics. Unchanged: message assembly (system + user prompt + a sliding window of the last history_n=5 screenshots), Thought/Action extraction, action-type detection. """ import ast import base64 import io import json import logging import logging.handlers import math import multiprocessing as mp import os import platform import random import re import shutil import tempfile import time import traceback import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET from datetime import datetime from glob import glob from io import BytesIO from time import sleep from typing import Dict, List import numpy as np from openai import OpenAI from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont from requests.exceptions import SSLError import prompts from runtime_config import get_config import web_controller import prompts RE_BOX_TOKEN = re.compile( r"<\|box_start\|>\s*" r"\(\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*,\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*\)" r"(?:\s*,\s*\(\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*,\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*\))?" r"\s*<\|box_end\|>", re.S, ) RE_START_BOX_STR = re.compile( r"start_box\s*=\s*'?\s*" r"\(\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*,\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*\)" r"(?:\s*,\s*\(\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*,\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*\))?" r"\s*'?", re.I, ) FINISH_WORD = "Finish" WAIT_WORD = "Wait" CALL_USER = "CallUser" IMAGE_FACTOR = 28 MIN_PIXELS = 100 * 28 * 28 MAX_PIXELS = 16384 * 28 * 28 # ── Size budget for screenshots sent to the model ───────────────────────── # Measured with a calibration page: when a 1920x1080 screenshot is sent as is, # the API first shrinks it to about 1440x810, and the model returns coordinates # in that *shrunken* space. Reading them as page coordinates put every click at # 75% of its target: # # send 1920x1080 -> clicks off by 122 / 158 / 189 px, all three targets missed # send 1440x810 -> clicks off by 1 / 1 / 5 px, all three hit # # Before this fix most tasks never finished: the agent kept clicking empty space. # The value is the largest size the API passes through without rescaling, so # coordinates map 1:1 onto the image we sent. The model's own pointing accuracy # (0-3 px) was never the problem. VLM_MAX_PIXELS = int(os.environ.get("WEBFOVEA_VLM_MAX_PIXELS", 1440 * 810)) MAX_RATIO = 200 def extract_between_keywords(text, start_key, end_key): pattern = re.compile(f'{re.escape(start_key)}(.*?){re.escape(end_key)}', re.DOTALL) matches = pattern.findall(text) return [match.strip() for match in matches] def parse_action(action_str): """Parse action string using ast (aligned with uitars15_v1).""" try: node = ast.parse(action_str, mode='eval') if not isinstance(node, ast.Expression): raise ValueError("Not an expression") call = node.body if not isinstance(call, ast.Call): raise ValueError("Not a function call") if isinstance(call.func, ast.Name): func_name = call.func.id elif isinstance(call.func, ast.Attribute): func_name = call.func.attr else: func_name = None kwargs = {} for kw in call.keywords: key = kw.arg if isinstance(kw.value, ast.Constant): value = kw.value.value elif isinstance(kw.value, ast.Str): # older Python versions value = kw.value.s else: value = None kwargs[key] = value return {'function': func_name, 'args': kwargs} except Exception as e: print(f"Failed to parse action '{action_str}': {e}") return None def escape_single_quotes(text): pattern = r"(? int: return round(number / factor) * factor def ceil_by_factor(number: int, factor: int) -> int: return math.ceil(number / factor) * factor def floor_by_factor(number: int, factor: int) -> int: return math.floor(number / factor) * factor def add_box_token(input_string): if "Action: " in input_string and "start_box=" in input_string: suffix = input_string.split("Action: ")[0] + "Action: " actions = input_string.split("Action: ")[1:] processed_actions = [] for action in actions: action = action.strip() coordinates = re.findall(r"(start_box|end_box)='\((\d+),\s*(\d+)\)'", action) updated_action = action for coord_type, x, y in coordinates: updated_action = updated_action.replace(f"{coord_type}='({x},{y})'", f"{coord_type}='<|box_start|>({x},{y})<|box_end|>'") processed_actions.append(updated_action) final_string = suffix + "\n\n".join(processed_actions) else: final_string = input_string return final_string def pil_to_base64(image): buffer = BytesIO() image.save(buffer, format="PNG") return base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode("utf-8") def linearize_accessibility_tree(accessibility_tree, platform="ubuntu"): if platform == "ubuntu": _attributes_ns = attributes_ns_ubuntu _state_ns = state_ns_ubuntu _component_ns = component_ns_ubuntu _value_ns = value_ns_ubuntu elif platform == "windows": _attributes_ns = attributes_ns_windows _state_ns = state_ns_windows _component_ns = component_ns_windows _value_ns = value_ns_windows else: raise ValueError("Invalid platform, must be 'ubuntu' or 'windows'") filtered_nodes = filter_nodes(ET.fromstring(accessibility_tree), platform) linearized_accessibility_tree = [ "tag\tname\ttext\tclass\tdescription\tposition (top-left x&y)\tsize (w&h)" ] for node in filtered_nodes: if node.text: text = ( node.text if '"' not in node.text else '"{:}"'.format(node.text.replace('"', '""')) ) elif node.get("{{{:}}}class".format(class_ns_windows), "").endswith( "EditWrapper" ) and node.get("{{{:}}}value".format(_value_ns)): node_text = node.get("{{{:}}}value".format(_value_ns), "") text = ( node_text if '"' not in node_text else '"{:}"'.format(node_text.replace('"', '""')) ) else: text = '""' linearized_accessibility_tree.append( "{:}\t{:}\t{:}\t{:}\t{:}\t{:}\t{:}".format( node.tag, node.get("name", ""), text, ( node.get("{{{:}}}class".format(_attributes_ns), "") if platform == "ubuntu" else node.get("{{{:}}}class".format(class_ns_windows), "") ), node.get("{{{:}}}description".format(_attributes_ns), ""), node.get("{{{:}}}screencoord".format(_component_ns), ""), node.get("{{{:}}}size".format(_component_ns), ""), ) ) return "\n".join(linearized_accessibility_tree) def trim_accessibility_tree(linearized_accessibility_tree, max_tokens): return linearized_accessibility_tree def get_start_index(base_directory): if not os.path.exists(base_directory): os.makedirs(base_directory, exist_ok=True) return 0 folders = [d for d in os.listdir(base_directory) if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(base_directory, d))] index_folders = [] for folder in folders: match = re.match(r'^(\d+)_', folder) if match: index = int(match.group(1)) index_folders.append((index, folder)) if not index_folders: return 0 max_index, max_folder = max(index_folders, key=lambda x: x[0]) folder_path = os.path.join(base_directory, max_folder) result_path = os.path.join(folder_path, 'result.json') if not os.path.exists(result_path): try: shutil.rmtree(folder_path) print(f"Removed folder without result.json: {folder_path}") except OSError as e: print(f"Failed to remove folder: {e}") return max_index return max_index + 1 def smart_resize( height: int, width: int, factor: int = IMAGE_FACTOR, min_pixels: int = MIN_PIXELS, max_pixels: int = MAX_PIXELS ) -> tuple[int, int]: """ Rescales the image so that the following conditions are met: 1. Both dimensions (height and width) are divisible by 'factor'. 2. The total number of pixels is within the range ['min_pixels', 'max_pixels']. 3. The aspect ratio of the image is maintained as closely as possible. """ if max(height, width) / min(height, width) > MAX_RATIO: raise ValueError( f"absolute aspect ratio must be smaller than {MAX_RATIO}, got {max(height, width) / min(height, width)}" ) h_bar = max(factor, round_by_factor(height, factor)) w_bar = max(factor, round_by_factor(width, factor)) if h_bar * w_bar > max_pixels: beta = math.sqrt((height * width) / max_pixels) h_bar = floor_by_factor(height / beta, factor) w_bar = floor_by_factor(width / beta, factor) elif h_bar * w_bar < min_pixels: beta = math.sqrt(min_pixels / (height * width)) h_bar = ceil_by_factor(height * beta, factor) w_bar = ceil_by_factor(width * beta, factor) return h_bar, w_bar def parse_action_to_structure_output(text, factor, origin_resized_height, origin_resized_width, model_type, max_pixels=16384*28*28, min_pixels=100*28*28, screen_width=None, screen_height=None): """Parse model output: extract thought, split actions, remap coordinates. Returns list of dicts: - text: full model output - thought: extracted thought string - raw_action: original action string as model output - action: action string with coordinates remapped to screen pixels - action_type: ast function name for terminal detection (finished/wait/call_user) """ text = text.strip() # Calculate smart_resize dimensions (what model actually sees) if model_type == "qwen25vl": smart_resize_height, smart_resize_width = smart_resize( origin_resized_height, origin_resized_width, factor=IMAGE_FACTOR, min_pixels=min_pixels, max_pixels=max_pixels) # Model coordinates -> real page pixels. # origin_resized_* is the size of the image *actually sent*; screen_* is the size # of the *real page (viewport)*. They differ whenever the screenshot was # downscaled, so they must be passed separately. The reference code treated them # as one value and divided by smart_resize (written for UI-TARS's 28-px patch # grid), which for Claude amounted to no mapping at all: every click was off by # a factor of 1.333. See the VLM_MAX_PIXELS comment at the top of this file. # # No factor is hard-coded on purpose: the viewport size depends on the browser # window (web_controller.open_page), so it can differ between machines and the # factor has to be computed every time. if screen_width is None: screen_width = origin_resized_width if screen_height is None: screen_height = origin_resized_height sent_width, sent_height = origin_resized_width, origin_resized_height # Coordinate remapping helper def remap_xy(x, y): """Convert model coordinates to screen pixels.""" rx = round(float(x) / sent_width * screen_width) ry = round(float(y) / sent_height * screen_height) return rx, ry def remap_action_str(raw_str): """Replace coordinates in action string with remapped screen pixel values.""" def replace_box_token(match): coord_type = match.group(1) x, y = match.group(2), match.group(3) rx, ry = remap_xy(x, y) return f"{coord_type}='<|box_start|>({rx},{ry})<|box_end|>'" def replace_simple(match): coord_type = match.group(1) x, y = match.group(2), match.group(3) rx, ry = remap_xy(x, y) return f"{coord_type}='({rx},{ry})'" # Handle <|box_start|>(x,y)<|box_end|> format first result = re.sub( r"(start_box|end_box)='<\|box_start\|>\((\d+),\s*(\d+)\)<\|box_end\|>'", replace_box_token, raw_str) # Then handle simple (x,y) format result = re.sub( r"(start_box|end_box)='\((\d+),\s*(\d+)\)'", replace_simple, result) # click_many(points='(x,y);(x,y);...'): remap every pair in the string def replace_points(match): def rp(m): rx, ry = remap_xy(m.group(1), m.group(2)) return f"({rx},{ry})" return "points='" + re.sub(r"\(\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*(\d+)\s*\)", rp, match.group(1)) + "'" result = re.sub(r"points='([^']*)'", replace_points, result) return result # 1. Extract thought if text.startswith("Thought:"): thought_pattern = r"Thought: (.+?)(?=\s*Action:|$)" elif text.startswith("Reflection:"): thought_pattern = r"Reflection: (.+?)Action_Summary: (.+?)(?=\s*Action:|$)" elif text.startswith("Action_Summary:"): thought_pattern = r"Action_Summary: (.+?)(?=\s*Action:|$)" else: thought_pattern = r"Thought: (.+?)(?=\s*Action:|$)" thought = None thought_match = re.search(thought_pattern, text, re.DOTALL) if thought_match: if len(thought_match.groups()) == 1: thought = thought_match.group(1).strip() elif len(thought_match.groups()) == 2: thought = thought_match.group(2).strip() assert "Action:" in text raw_action_str = text.split("Action:")[-1].strip() # Drop anything after the action. In one run the model followed every action with # "\n
"; finished(content='...')\n
then failed ast parsing, the fallback regex # requires a trailing ")", and a correct answer came out as an empty agent_answer. # Cutting at the last ")" leaves parentheses inside the answer intact. m = re.match(r"(?s)^(\w+\(.*\))", raw_action_str) if m: raw_action_str = m.group(1) if "type(content" in raw_action_str: def escape_quotes(match): return match.group(1) pattern = r"type\(content='(.*?)'\)" content = re.sub(pattern, escape_quotes, raw_action_str) type_str = escape_single_quotes(content) raw_action_str = "type(content='" + type_str + "')" raw_action_str = raw_action_str.strip() remapped_action_str = remap_action_str(raw_action_str) result = { "text": text, "thought": thought, "raw_action": raw_action_str, # action string as the model wrote it "action": remapped_action_str, # same, with coordinates mapped to page pixels } return result def _log_usage(agent, response, started_at, attempt): """Log the token usage of one model call to the worker log. **Off by default.** It must never affect the run itself: the whole body is wrapped in try and every exception is swallowed. A diagnostic that breaks the real work is the worst possible trade. Why log it at all: `response.usage` used to be discarded, so there was no way to tell whether prompt caching kicked in. Reading the code suggests it does not (the history_n=5 image window shifts every step, rewriting the middle of the message list, and the OpenAI-compatible endpoint receives no cache_control). At a few hundred dollars per 100-task run, that is worth confirming with data. Uses the logger rather than a separate file: no plumbing changes, and the worker log is already split per task. """ try: if not get_config().log_usage: return u = getattr(response, "usage", None) if u is None: return try: data = u.model_dump() # pydantic: includes the cache-related extension fields except Exception: data = {k: getattr(u, k, None) for k in ("prompt_tokens", "completion_tokens", "total_tokens")} data["elapsed_s"] = round(time.time() - started_at, 2) data["attempt"] = attempt + 1 data["model"] = getattr(response, "model", None) data["finish_reason"] = response.choices[0].finish_reason if response.choices else None data["n_messages"] = len(agent.history_responses) * 2 + 3 # rough; for watching context growth if agent.logger: agent.logger.info("[usage] " + json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False)) except Exception: pass #: The model occasionally emits **chat-template end tokens** (`<|eot_id|>` 471 times, #: `<|end_of_turn|>` 80 times in our logs), most likely imitating the `<|box_start|>` #: notation in the prompt. They have to be stripped here because they do damage in #: two ways, and the second is the fatal one: #: 1. Left inside `type(content=...)`, the token is **typed into the input box as #: text**. One episode typed `2022 June<|end_of_turn|>` into a filter box and the #: site kept answering "No Results". The model even diagnosed this in its own #: thoughts ("the type command keeps appending ... to the text") but could not #: get around it. #: 2. The reply goes into `history_responses` unchanged, so on the next step the #: model sees itself using the token and keeps doing it. It hit 15 of 305 #: episodes (4.9%); every one started at step 0, carried the token on every step #: after that, and scored zero, and 14 of them never called finished() at all. #: Only the box tokens used for coordinates are let through; everything else is cut. #: A regex rather than a fixed list: adding tokens one at a time (`<|im_end|>` was #: handled that way) always left others uncovered. _SPECIAL_TOKEN = re.compile(r"<\|(?!box_start\|>|box_end\|>)[A-Za-z0-9_]+\|>") def _truncate_to_first_action(text: str) -> str: """Keep only the first Thought/Action pair and drop the turns the model made up. The model often invents a whole interaction in a single reply: Thought: Let me click the "Confirmed Planets" link first. Action: click(...) The screenshot has changed after the action. Thought: ... Action: scroll(...) ... Action: finished(content='14') <- made up without ever seeing the page parse_action searched the *whole* text for an action, and any `finished(` ended the task, so the agent could submit a fabricated answer at step 0 (one task was answered 14 when the truth was 34). That is far worse than giving no answer. The same place also strips self-generated chat-template tokens; see _SPECIAL_TOKEN. """ if not text: return text # Markers the model uses to fake "the environment sent me a new screenshot" for marker in ("", ""): idx = text.find(marker) if idx != -1: text = text[:idx] # Self-generated special tokens (`<|eot_id|>` etc.): cut at the first one, along with everything after it m = _SPECIAL_TOKEN.search(text) if m: text = text[:m.start()] # No marker: fall back to cutting at the first Thought that follows the first Action first_action = text.find("Action:") if first_action != -1: nxt = text.find("Thought:", first_action) if nxt != -1: text = text[:nxt] return text.strip() def _obs_content(encoded_image: str, note: str = None): """Message content for the current observation. If the executor reported that the last action had no effect (web_controller.LAST_ACTION_NOTE), a text note goes in front of the screenshot. Without it a silently failed action is invisible to the model: it only sees an unchanged screenshot and repeats the action until the step budget runs out.""" content = [] if note: content.append({ "type": "text", "text": f"[Action feedback] {note}", }) content.append({ "type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{encoded_image}"}, }) return content class UITARSAgent: """UI-TARS 1.5 Agent - VLM-based GUI agent (aligned with uitars15_v1, no runtime_conf).""" def __init__( self, model: str = "uitars", api_url: str = "http://localhost:8001/v1", api_key: str = None, model_type: str = "qwen25vl", platform: str = "ubuntu", action_space: str = "pyautogui", observation_type: str = "screenshot", max_trajectory_length: int = 50, a11y_tree_max_tokens: int = 10000, temperature: float = 0.7, top_k: int = -1, top_p: float = 1.0, max_tokens: int = 8192, history_n: int = 5, max_pixels: int = VLM_MAX_PIXELS, # measured limit, see the comment at the top of this file min_pixels: int = 100 * 28 * 28, language: str = "Chinese", infer_mode: str = "qwen2vl_user", prompt_style: str = "qwen2vl_user", input_swap: bool = True, callusr_tolerance: int = 0, ): if api_key is None: api_key = os.getenv("VLM_API_KEY", "EMPTY") # max_retries=0 turns off the SDK's own retries; stacked on top of the backoff in # predict(), they made the time spent on a failing call unpredictable. self.vlm = OpenAI(base_url=api_url, api_key=api_key, timeout=120.0, max_retries=0) self.model = model self.model_type = model_type self.platform = platform self.action_space = action_space self.observation_type = observation_type self.max_trajectory_length = max_trajectory_length self.a11y_tree_max_tokens = a11y_tree_max_tokens self.temperature = temperature self.top_k = top_k self.top_p = top_p self.max_tokens = max_tokens self.history_n = history_n self.max_pixels = max_pixels self.min_pixels = min_pixels self.language = language self.infer_mode = infer_mode self.prompt_style = prompt_style self.input_swap = input_swap self.callusr_tolerance = callusr_tolerance self.action_parse_res_factor = 1000 # Select action space based on infer_mode (from prompts module) self.prompt_action_space = prompts.UITARS_ACTION_SPACE if self.infer_mode == "qwen2vl_user": self.prompt_action_space = prompts.UITARS_CALL_USR_ACTION_SPACE elif self.infer_mode == "qwen25vl_normal": # Whether each added action (back / find_text / read_text / fill / click_many / # the answer-provenance rule) appears in the action space is set by switches in # config.json; see prompts.normal_action_space(). A function rather than a # constant, so "switched off means the model never sees it" can be tested. _cfg = get_config() self.prompt_action_space = prompts.normal_action_space( _cfg.enable_back, _cfg.enable_find_text, _cfg.enable_read_text, _cfg.enable_fill, _cfg.enable_provenance_rule, _cfg.enable_click_many) # Select prompt template based on prompt_style (from prompts module) self.prompt_template = prompts.UITARS_USR_PROMPT_THOUGHT if self.prompt_style in ("qwen2vl_user", "qwen25vl_normal"): self.prompt_template = prompts.UITARS_USR_PROMPT_THOUGHT elif self.prompt_style == "qwen2vl_no_thought": self.prompt_template = prompts.UITARS_USR_PROMPT_NOTHOUGHT self.thoughts = [] self.actions = [] self.observations = [] self.history_images = [] self.history_responses = [] self.urls = [] self.logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) self.cur_callusr_count = 0 def reset(self): self.thoughts = [] self.actions = [] self.observations = [] self.history_images = [] self.history_responses = [] self.urls = [] self.cur_callusr_count = 0 def predict( self, instruction: str, obs: Dict, last_action_after_obs: Dict = None ) -> List: """ Predict the next action(s) based on the current observation. """ # Flow: record this step's screenshot -> build messages (prompt + recent screenshots # + past replies + current screenshot) -> call the model (with retries) -> clean the # reply -> parse the action and map coordinates -> record history -> check for the end # Append trajectory assert len(self.observations) == len(self.actions) and len(self.actions) == len( self.thoughts ), "The number of observations and actions should be the same." if len(self.observations) > self.max_trajectory_length: if self.max_trajectory_length == 0: _observations = [] _actions = [] _thoughts = [] else: _observations = self.observations[-self.max_trajectory_length :] _actions = self.actions[-self.max_trajectory_length :] _thoughts = self.thoughts[-self.max_trajectory_length :] else: _observations = self.observations _actions = self.actions _thoughts = self.thoughts self.history_images.append(obs["screenshot"]) if self.observation_type in ["screenshot", "screenshot_a11y_tree"]: base64_image = obs["screenshot"] try: linearized_accessibility_tree = ( linearize_accessibility_tree( accessibility_tree=obs["accessibility_tree"], platform=self.platform, ) if self.observation_type == "screenshot_a11y_tree" else None ) except: linearized_accessibility_tree = None if linearized_accessibility_tree: linearized_accessibility_tree = trim_accessibility_tree( linearized_accessibility_tree, self.a11y_tree_max_tokens ) if self.observation_type == "screenshot_a11y_tree": self.observations.append( { "screenshot": base64_image, "accessibility_tree": linearized_accessibility_tree, } ) else: self.observations.append( {"screenshot": base64_image, "accessibility_tree": None} ) else: raise ValueError( "Invalid observation_type type: " + self.observation_type ) if self.infer_mode == "qwen2vl_user" or self.infer_mode == "qwen25vl_normal": user_prompt = self.prompt_template.format( instruction=instruction, action_space=self.prompt_action_space, language=self.language ) elif self.infer_mode == "qwen2vl_no_thought": user_prompt = self.prompt_template.format( instruction=instruction ) if len(self.history_images) > self.history_n: self.history_images = self.history_images[-self.history_n:] messages, images = [], [] if isinstance(self.history_images, bytes): self.history_images = [self.history_images] elif isinstance(self.history_images, np.ndarray): self.history_images = list(self.history_images) elif isinstance(self.history_images, list): pass else: raise TypeError(f"Unidentified images type: {type(self.history_images)}") for turn, image in enumerate(self.history_images): if len(images) >= self.history_n: break try: image = Image.open(BytesIO(image)) except Exception as e: raise RuntimeError(f"Error opening image: {e}") # The size before downscaling is the real page (viewport) size, the space # coordinates must be mapped back to. The loop runs oldest to newest, so the # last image is the current step's screenshot. page_width, page_height = image.width, image.height if image.width * image.height > self.max_pixels: resize_factor = math.sqrt(self.max_pixels / (image.width * image.height)) width, height = int(image.width * resize_factor), int(image.height * resize_factor) image = image.resize((width, height)) if image.width * image.height < self.min_pixels: resize_factor = math.sqrt(self.min_pixels / (image.width * image.height)) width, height = math.ceil(image.width * resize_factor), math.ceil(image.height * resize_factor) image = image.resize((width, height)) if image.mode != "RGB": image = image.convert("RGB") images.append(image) messages = [ { "role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "You are a helpful assistant."}] }, { "role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": user_prompt}] } ] image_num = 0 if len(self.history_responses) > 0: for history_idx, history_response in enumerate(self.history_responses): # send at most history_n images to the model if history_idx + self.history_n > len(self.history_responses): cur_image = images[image_num] encoded_string = pil_to_base64(cur_image) messages.append({ "role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{encoded_string}"}}] }) image_num += 1 messages.append({ "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": add_box_token(history_response)}] }) cur_image = images[image_num] encoded_string = pil_to_base64(cur_image) messages.append({ "role": "user", "content": _obs_content(encoded_string, obs.get("note")) }) image_num += 1 else: cur_image = images[image_num] encoded_string = pil_to_base64(cur_image) messages.append({ "role": "user", "content": _obs_content(encoded_string, obs.get("note")) }) image_num += 1 # Size of the image actually sent (possibly downscaled by the max_pixels budget) origin_resized_height = images[-1].height origin_resized_width = images[-1].width if origin_resized_width != page_width: print(f"[coord] screenshot {page_width}x{page_height} -> sent " f"{origin_resized_width}x{origin_resized_height}, " f"coordinate scale {page_width / origin_resized_width:.4f}") temperature = self.temperature top_k = self.top_k prediction = None # Attempts and total time are configurable; see runtime_config.model_call_max_attempts # (with a fixed 3 attempts, three 403s in a row at step 0 ended a task before it began). _cfg = get_config() max_retries = max(1, _cfg.model_call_max_attempts) _retry_started = time.time() for attempt in range(max_retries): try: _call_started = time.time() response = self.vlm.chat.completions.create( model=self.model, messages=messages, frequency_penalty=1, max_tokens=self.max_tokens, temperature=temperature ) _log_usage(self, response, _call_started, attempt) print("*" * 20) print("Response:") print(response.choices[0].message.content) print("*" * 20) prediction = _truncate_to_first_action( response.choices[0].message.content.strip()) break except Exception as e: # 429 rate limits, 5xx and network timeouts are worth a retry; other 4xx # errors (bad parameters) are not. 403 is the exception: we saw sporadic # `403 Request not allowed` responses mid-task, each of which used to kill # the task on the spot (2 of 10 tasks in one run). They are transient # policy refusals that usually pass on retry; treating them like a 400 for # a malformed request was far too harsh. status_code = getattr(e, "status_code", None) retryable = (status_code is None or status_code == 429 or status_code == 403 or status_code >= 500) self.logger.warning( f"Model call failed (attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_retries}, status={status_code}): {e}") if (not retryable or attempt == max_retries - 1 or time.time() - _retry_started > _cfg.model_call_retry_budget_s): break # 403/429 usually clear within seconds; cap the wait at 30 s per attempt time.sleep(min(2 ** attempt * 2, 30)) if prediction is None: # This used to return ["DONE"] (a list), which main.py's `condition in ["DONE"]` # never matched, so the task idled until the step limit. A failed model call fails # the task; end it quickly and leave the time to other tasks. return "client error", "FAIL" # Parse model output → browser-ready action dicts (one step) try: parsed_response = parse_action_to_structure_output( prediction, self.action_parse_res_factor, origin_resized_height, origin_resized_width, self.model_type, self.max_pixels, self.min_pixels, screen_width=page_width, # real page size, not the size sent screen_height=page_height, ) except Exception as e: print(f"Parsing action error: {prediction}, with error:\n{e}") # Same as above: a list slips past main.py's check. Parsing failed, so fail fast return f"Parsing action error: {prediction}, with error:\n{e}", "FAIL" # Record history thought_str = parsed_response["thought"] action_str = parsed_response["action"] self.thoughts.append(thought_str) self.actions.append(action_str) self.history_responses.append(prediction) # Collect browser actions, check for terminal conditions action_type = web_controller.parse_action_type(action_str) if action_type == FINISH_WORD: return prediction, "DONE" elif action_type == WAIT_WORD: return prediction, "WAIT" elif action_type == CALL_USER: if self.callusr_tolerance > self.cur_callusr_count: self.cur_callusr_count += 1 return prediction, "WAIT" else: return prediction, "FAIL" if len(self.history_responses) >= self.max_trajectory_length: return prediction, "FAIL" return prediction, "CONTINUE" def get_thoughts(self): return self.thoughts def get_actions(self): return self.actions def get_history_responses(self): return self.history_responses def get_history_images(self): return self.history_images def get_urls(self): return self.urls

"""Model layer: screenshot -> messages -> model call -> parsed action -> page pixels. Starts from the UI-TARS 1.5 reference implementation. What changed, in the order a step goes through it: 1. Screenshot size VLM_MAX_PIXELS / UITARSAgent.predict() Screenshots larger than 1440x810 are downscaled before sending. Otherwise the API downscales them itself, the model answers in the downscaled image's coordinates, and the reference code read those as page coordinates, so every click landed at 3/4 of its target. 2. Coordinate mapping parse_action_to_structure_output() The size of the image actually sent and the real viewport size are passed separately: page pixel = model coordinate x (viewport / sent). 3. Reply cleanup _truncate_to_first_action() / _SPECIAL_TOKEN Keep only the first Thought/Action pair (the model likes to invent the rest of the conversation, fake finished() included); strip self-generated chat-template tokens such as <|eot_id|>; drop trailing junk after the action (e.g. "
"). 4. Action feedback _obs_content() When the executor reports that the last action had no effect or was rejected, that note is sent to the model in front of the screenshot. 5. Model-call retries UITARSAgent.predict() Back off and retry on 403 / 429 / 5xx / timeouts; attempts and total time are set in config.json. A final failure returns ("client error", "FAIL") so the main loop ends the task quickly and still writes result.json. 6. Usage logging _log_usage(), off by default; for local diagnostics. Unchanged: message assembly (system + user prompt + a sliding window of the last history_n=5 screenshots), Thought/Action extraction, action-type detection. """ import ast import base64 import io import json import logging import logging.handlers import math import multiprocessing as mp import os import platform import random import re import shutil import tempfile import time import traceback import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET from datetime import datetime from glob import glob from io import BytesIO from time import sleep from typing import Dict, List import numpy as np from openai import OpenAI from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont from requests.exceptions import SSLError import prompts from runtime_config import get_config import web_controller import prompts RE_BOX_TOKEN = re.compile( r"<\|box_start\|>\s*" r"\(\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*,\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*\)" r"(?:\s*,\s*\(\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*,\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*\))?" r"\s*<\|box_end\|>", re.S, ) RE_START_BOX_STR = re.compile( r"start_box\s*=\s*'?\s*" r"\(\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*,\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*\)" r"(?:\s*,\s*\(\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*,\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*\))?" r"\s*'?", re.I, ) FINISH_WORD = "Finish" WAIT_WORD = "Wait" CALL_USER = "CallUser" IMAGE_FACTOR = 28 MIN_PIXELS = 100 * 28 * 28 MAX_PIXELS = 16384 * 28 * 28 # ── Size budget for screenshots sent to the model ───────────────────────── # Measured with a calibration page: when a 1920x1080 screenshot is sent as is, # the API first shrinks it to about 1440x810, and the model returns coordinates # in that *shrunken* space. Reading them as page coordinates put every click at # 75% of its target: # # send 1920x1080 -> clicks off by 122 / 158 / 189 px, all three targets missed # send 1440x810 -> clicks off by 1 / 1 / 5 px, all three hit # # Before this fix most tasks never finished: the agent kept clicking empty space. # The value is the largest size the API passes through without rescaling, so # coordinates map 1:1 onto the image we sent. The model's own pointing accuracy # (0-3 px) was never the problem. VLM_MAX_PIXELS = int(os.environ.get("WEBFOVEA_VLM_MAX_PIXELS", 1440 * 810)) MAX_RATIO = 200 def extract_between_keywords(text, start_key, end_key): pattern = re.compile(f'{re.escape(start_key)}(.*?){re.escape(end_key)}', re.DOTALL) matches = pattern.findall(text) return [match.strip() for match in matches] def parse_action(action_str): """Parse action string using ast (aligned with uitars15_v1).""" try: node = ast.parse(action_str, mode='eval') if not isinstance(node, ast.Expression): raise ValueError("Not an expression") call = node.body if not isinstance(call, ast.Call): raise ValueError("Not a function call") if isinstance(call.func, ast.Name): func_name = call.func.id elif isinstance(call.func, ast.Attribute): func_name = call.func.attr else: func_name = None kwargs = {} for kw in call.keywords: key = kw.arg if isinstance(kw.value, ast.Constant): value = kw.value.value elif isinstance(kw.value, ast.Str): # older Python versions value = kw.value.s else: value = None kwargs[key] = value return {'function': func_name, 'args': kwargs} except Exception as e: print(f"Failed to parse action '{action_str}': {e}") return None def escape_single_quotes(text): pattern = r"(? int: return round(number / factor) * factor def ceil_by_factor(number: int, factor: int) -> int: return math.ceil(number / factor) * factor def floor_by_factor(number: int, factor: int) -> int: return math.floor(number / factor) * factor def add_box_token(input_string): if "Action: " in input_string and "start_box=" in input_string: suffix = input_string.split("Action: ")[0] + "Action: " actions = input_string.split("Action: ")[1:] processed_actions = [] for action in actions: action = action.strip() coordinates = re.findall(r"(start_box|end_box)='\((\d+),\s*(\d+)\)'", action) updated_action = action for coord_type, x, y in coordinates: updated_action = updated_action.replace(f"{coord_type}='({x},{y})'", f"{coord_type}='<|box_start|>({x},{y})<|box_end|>'") processed_actions.append(updated_action) final_string = suffix + "\n\n".join(processed_actions) else: final_string = input_string return final_string def pil_to_base64(image): buffer = BytesIO() image.save(buffer, format="PNG") return base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode("utf-8") def linearize_accessibility_tree(accessibility_tree, platform="ubuntu"): if platform == "ubuntu": _attributes_ns = attributes_ns_ubuntu _state_ns = state_ns_ubuntu _component_ns = component_ns_ubuntu _value_ns = value_ns_ubuntu elif platform == "windows": _attributes_ns = attributes_ns_windows _state_ns = state_ns_windows _component_ns = component_ns_windows _value_ns = value_ns_windows else: raise ValueError("Invalid platform, must be 'ubuntu' or 'windows'") filtered_nodes = filter_nodes(ET.fromstring(accessibility_tree), platform) linearized_accessibility_tree = [ "tag\tname\ttext\tclass\tdescription\tposition (top-left x&y)\tsize (w&h)" ] for node in filtered_nodes: if node.text: text = ( node.text if '"' not in node.text else '"{:}"'.format(node.text.replace('"', '""')) ) elif node.get("{{{:}}}class".format(class_ns_windows), "").endswith( "EditWrapper" ) and node.get("{{{:}}}value".format(_value_ns)): node_text = node.get("{{{:}}}value".format(_value_ns), "") text = ( node_text if '"' not in node_text else '"{:}"'.format(node_text.replace('"', '""')) ) else: text = '""' linearized_accessibility_tree.append( "{:}\t{:}\t{:}\t{:}\t{:}\t{:}\t{:}".format( node.tag, node.get("name", ""), text, ( node.get("{{{:}}}class".format(_attributes_ns), "") if platform == "ubuntu" else node.get("{{{:}}}class".format(class_ns_windows), "") ), node.get("{{{:}}}description".format(_attributes_ns), ""), node.get("{{{:}}}screencoord".format(_component_ns), ""), node.get("{{{:}}}size".format(_component_ns), ""), ) ) return "\n".join(linearized_accessibility_tree) def trim_accessibility_tree(linearized_accessibility_tree, max_tokens): return linearized_accessibility_tree def get_start_index(base_directory): if not os.path.exists(base_directory): os.makedirs(base_directory, exist_ok=True) return 0 folders = [d for d in os.listdir(base_directory) if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(base_directory, d))] index_folders = [] for folder in folders: match = re.match(r'^(\d+)_', folder) if match: index = int(match.group(1)) index_folders.append((index, folder)) if not index_folders: return 0 max_index, max_folder = max(index_folders, key=lambda x: x[0]) folder_path = os.path.join(base_directory, max_folder) result_path = os.path.join(folder_path, 'result.json') if not os.path.exists(result_path): try: shutil.rmtree(folder_path) print(f"Removed folder without result.json: {folder_path}") except OSError as e: print(f"Failed to remove folder: {e}") return max_index return max_index + 1 def smart_resize( height: int, width: int, factor: int = IMAGE_FACTOR, min_pixels: int = MIN_PIXELS, max_pixels: int = MAX_PIXELS ) -> tuple[int, int]: """ Rescales the image so that the following conditions are met: 1. Both dimensions (height and width) are divisible by 'factor'. 2. The total number of pixels is within the range ['min_pixels', 'max_pixels']. 3. The aspect ratio of the image is maintained as closely as possible. """ if max(height, width) / min(height, width) > MAX_RATIO: raise ValueError( f"absolute aspect ratio must be smaller than {MAX_RATIO}, got {max(height, width) / min(height, width)}" ) h_bar = max(factor, round_by_factor(height, factor)) w_bar = max(factor, round_by_factor(width, factor)) if h_bar * w_bar > max_pixels: beta = math.sqrt((height * width) / max_pixels) h_bar = floor_by_factor(height / beta, factor) w_bar = floor_by_factor(width / beta, factor) elif h_bar * w_bar < min_pixels: beta = math.sqrt(min_pixels / (height * width)) h_bar = ceil_by_factor(height * beta, factor) w_bar = ceil_by_factor(width * beta, factor) return h_bar, w_bar def parse_action_to_structure_output(text, factor, origin_resized_height, origin_resized_width, model_type, max_pixels=16384*28*28, min_pixels=100*28*28, screen_width=None, screen_height=None): """Parse model output: extract thought, split actions, remap coordinates. Returns list of dicts: - text: full model output - thought: extracted thought string - raw_action: original action string as model output - action: action string with coordinates remapped to screen pixels - action_type: ast function name for terminal detection (finished/wait/call_user) """ text = text.strip() # Calculate smart_resize dimensions (what model actually sees) if model_type == "qwen25vl": smart_resize_height, smart_resize_width = smart_resize( origin_resized_height, origin_resized_width, factor=IMAGE_FACTOR, min_pixels=min_pixels, max_pixels=max_pixels) # Model coordinates -> real page pixels. # origin_resized_* is the size of the image *actually sent*; screen_* is the size # of the *real page (viewport)*. They differ whenever the screenshot was # downscaled, so they must be passed separately. The reference code treated them # as one value and divided by smart_resize (written for UI-TARS's 28-px patch # grid), which for Claude amounted to no mapping at all: every click was off by # a factor of 1.333. See the VLM_MAX_PIXELS comment at the top of this file. # # No factor is hard-coded on purpose: the viewport size depends on the browser # window (web_controller.open_page), so it can differ between machines and the # factor has to be computed every time. if screen_width is None: screen_width = origin_resized_width if screen_height is None: screen_height = origin_resized_height sent_width, sent_height = origin_resized_width, origin_resized_height # Coordinate remapping helper def remap_xy(x, y): """Convert model coordinates to screen pixels.""" rx = round(float(x) / sent_width * screen_width) ry = round(float(y) / sent_height * screen_height) return rx, ry def remap_action_str(raw_str): """Replace coordinates in action string with remapped screen pixel values.""" def replace_box_token(match): coord_type = match.group(1) x, y = match.group(2), match.group(3) rx, ry = remap_xy(x, y) return f"{coord_type}='<|box_start|>({rx},{ry})<|box_end|>'" def replace_simple(match): coord_type = match.group(1) x, y = match.group(2), match.group(3) rx, ry = remap_xy(x, y) return f"{coord_type}='({rx},{ry})'" # Handle <|box_start|>(x,y)<|box_end|> format first result = re.sub( r"(start_box|end_box)='<\|box_start\|>\((\d+),\s*(\d+)\)<\|box_end\|>'", replace_box_token, raw_str) # Then handle simple (x,y) format result = re.sub( r"(start_box|end_box)='\((\d+),\s*(\d+)\)'", replace_simple, result) # click_many(points='(x,y);(x,y);...'): remap every pair in the string def replace_points(match): def rp(m): rx, ry = remap_xy(m.group(1), m.group(2)) return f"({rx},{ry})" return "points='" + re.sub(r"\(\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*(\d+)\s*\)", rp, match.group(1)) + "'" result = re.sub(r"points='([^']*)'", replace_points, result) return result # 1. Extract thought if text.startswith("Thought:"): thought_pattern = r"Thought: (.+?)(?=\s*Action:|$)" elif text.startswith("Reflection:"): thought_pattern = r"Reflection: (.+?)Action_Summary: (.+?)(?=\s*Action:|$)" elif text.startswith("Action_Summary:"): thought_pattern = r"Action_Summary: (.+?)(?=\s*Action:|$)" else: thought_pattern = r"Thought: (.+?)(?=\s*Action:|$)" thought = None thought_match = re.search(thought_pattern, text, re.DOTALL) if thought_match: if len(thought_match.groups()) == 1: thought = thought_match.group(1).strip() elif len(thought_match.groups()) == 2: thought = thought_match.group(2).strip() assert "Action:" in text raw_action_str = text.split("Action:")[-1].strip() # Drop anything after the action. In one run the model followed every action with # "\n
"; finished(content='...')\n
then failed ast parsing, the fallback regex # requires a trailing ")", and a correct answer came out as an empty agent_answer. # Cutting at the last ")" leaves parentheses inside the answer intact. m = re.match(r"(?s)^(\w+\(.*\))", raw_action_str) if m: raw_action_str = m.group(1) if "type(content" in raw_action_str: def escape_quotes(match): return match.group(1) pattern = r"type\(content='(.*?)'\)" content = re.sub(pattern, escape_quotes, raw_action_str) type_str = escape_single_quotes(content) raw_action_str = "type(content='" + type_str + "')" raw_action_str = raw_action_str.strip() remapped_action_str = remap_action_str(raw_action_str) result = { "text": text, "thought": thought, "raw_action": raw_action_str, # action string as the model wrote it "action": remapped_action_str, # same, with coordinates mapped to page pixels } return result def _log_usage(agent, response, started_at, attempt): """Log the token usage of one model call to the worker log. **Off by default.** It must never affect the run itself: the whole body is wrapped in try and every exception is swallowed. A diagnostic that breaks the real work is the worst possible trade. Why log it at all: `response.usage` used to be discarded, so there was no way to tell whether prompt caching kicked in. Reading the code suggests it does not (the history_n=5 image window shifts every step, rewriting the middle of the message list, and the OpenAI-compatible endpoint receives no cache_control). At a few hundred dollars per 100-task run, that is worth confirming with data. Uses the logger rather than a separate file: no plumbing changes, and the worker log is already split per task. """ try: if not get_config().log_usage: return u = getattr(response, "usage", None) if u is None: return try: data = u.model_dump() # pydantic: includes the cache-related extension fields except Exception: data = {k: getattr(u, k, None) for k in ("prompt_tokens", "completion_tokens", "total_tokens")} data["elapsed_s"] = round(time.time() - started_at, 2) data["attempt"] = attempt + 1 data["model"] = getattr(response, "model", None) data["finish_reason"] = response.choices[0].finish_reason if response.choices else None data["n_messages"] = len(agent.history_responses) * 2 + 3 # rough; for watching context growth if agent.logger: agent.logger.info("[usage] " + json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False)) except Exception: pass #: The model occasionally emits **chat-template end tokens** (`<|eot_id|>` 471 times, #: `<|end_of_turn|>` 80 times in our logs), most likely imitating the `<|box_start|>` #: notation in the prompt. They have to be stripped here because they do damage in #: two ways, and the second is the fatal one: #: 1. Left inside `type(content=...)`, the token is **typed into the input box as #: text**. One episode typed `2022 June<|end_of_turn|>` into a filter box and the #: site kept answering "No Results". The model even diagnosed this in its own #: thoughts ("the type command keeps appending ... to the text") but could not #: get around it. #: 2. The reply goes into `history_responses` unchanged, so on the next step the #: model sees itself using the token and keeps doing it. It hit 15 of 305 #: episodes (4.9%); every one started at step 0, carried the token on every step #: after that, and scored zero, and 14 of them never called finished() at all. #: Only the box tokens used for coordinates are let through; everything else is cut. #: A regex rather than a fixed list: adding tokens one at a time (`<|im_end|>` was #: handled that way) always left others uncovered. _SPECIAL_TOKEN = re.compile(r"<\|(?!box_start\|>|box_end\|>)[A-Za-z0-9_]+\|>") def _truncate_to_first_action(text: str) -> str: """Keep only the first Thought/Action pair and drop the turns the model made up. The model often invents a whole interaction in a single reply: Thought: Let me click the "Confirmed Planets" link first. Action: click(...) The screenshot has changed after the action. Thought: ... Action: scroll(...) ... Action: finished(content='14') <- made up without ever seeing the page parse_action searched the *whole* text for an action, and any `finished(` ended the task, so the agent could submit a fabricated answer at step 0 (one task was answered 14 when the truth was 34). That is far worse than giving no answer. The same place also strips self-generated chat-template tokens; see _SPECIAL_TOKEN. """ if not text: return text # Markers the model uses to fake "the environment sent me a new screenshot" for marker in ("", ""): idx = text.find(marker) if idx != -1: text = text[:idx] # Self-generated special tokens (`<|eot_id|>` etc.): cut at the first one, along with everything after it m = _SPECIAL_TOKEN.search(text) if m: text = text[:m.start()] # No marker: fall back to cutting at the first Thought that follows the first Action first_action = text.find("Action:") if first_action != -1: nxt = text.find("Thought:", first_action) if nxt != -1: text = text[:nxt] return text.strip() def _obs_content(encoded_image: str, note: str = None): """Message content for the current observation. If the executor reported that the last action had no effect (web_controller.LAST_ACTION_NOTE), a text note goes in front of the screenshot. Without it a silently failed action is invisible to the model: it only sees an unchanged screenshot and repeats the action until the step budget runs out.""" content = [] if note: content.append({ "type": "text", "text": f"[Action feedback] {note}", }) content.append({ "type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{encoded_image}"}, }) return content class UITARSAgent: """UI-TARS 1.5 Agent - VLM-based GUI agent (aligned with uitars15_v1, no runtime_conf).""" def __init__( self, model: str = "uitars", api_url: str = "http://localhost:8001/v1", api_key: str = None, model_type: str = "qwen25vl", platform: str = "ubuntu", action_space: str = "pyautogui", observation_type: str = "screenshot", max_trajectory_length: int = 50, a11y_tree_max_tokens: int = 10000, temperature: float = 0.7, top_k: int = -1, top_p: float = 1.0, max_tokens: int = 8192, history_n: int = 5, max_pixels: int = VLM_MAX_PIXELS, # measured limit, see the comment at the top of this file min_pixels: int = 100 * 28 * 28, language: str = "Chinese", infer_mode: str = "qwen2vl_user", prompt_style: str = "qwen2vl_user", input_swap: bool = True, callusr_tolerance: int = 0, ): if api_key is None: api_key = os.getenv("VLM_API_KEY", "EMPTY") # max_retries=0 turns off the SDK's own retries; """Browser layer: connect, open pages, execute actions, record network requests.

Starts from the reference implementation; init_playwright_context() and its
authentication-header logic are kept as they were. Changes, in call order:

  Open      open_page()
     - Single-tab reset, close_other_pages(): each task keeps only its own tab. The
       new tab is created before the old ones are closed, so at least one page
       exists at all times (closing the last page also closes a CDP-connected browser).
     - First-paint wait, settle_after_navigation(): floor -> early exit -> ceiling,
       instead of a blind fixed 3-second wait.
  Parse     parse_action() / parse_action_type()
     Adds hover / select / fill / reload / back / find_text / read_text / click_many.
     goto is still parsed, but only so the executor can reject it.
  Execute   excute_action(), the same sequence for every action:
     fingerprint before -> dispatch by action name -> handle newly opened tabs ->
     wait for rendering -> compare fingerprints to detect a no-op
     - Feedback channel LAST_ACTION_NOTE: when an action is rejected, fails or has no
       effect, a sentence is recorded and the main loop passes it to the model.
       Without it a silently failed action is invisible to the model, which then
       repeats it until the step budget runs out.
     - No-op detection, page_fingerprint(): compares a DOM fingerprint (url / title /
       node count / text length / scroll offsets / focus), which ignores clocks and
       carousels; when nothing changed, the model is told plainly not to repeat itself.
     - iframe fallback, child_frame_hit() / js_click_in_frame(): when a click lands in
       an iframe, the child frame's fingerprint decides whether it worked; if the
       physical click was swallowed, DOM events are dispatched inside the child frame
       (except in CAPTCHA frames).
     - Hard blocks: browser-level shortcuts (ctrl+l / F5 ...) and goto are always
       rejected, with the reason.
     - Per-task budgets (rejected with a reason once exceeded): reload <= 2,
       back <= 15, find_text <= 10, read_text <= 5, click_many <= 6. Reset at the
       start of each task by reset_stall_counters().
  Record    RequestCollector
     attach() is idempotent and clear() unbinds before emptying, so capture.json
     holds only the current task's requests.

Boundaries: the agent reaches answers only by operating the page. find_text only
scrolls and never reads a value; read_text reads DOM text from the page as currently
rendered; click_many counts one step per click. goto, search engines and hand-built
API URLs are never used, and the executor rejects them outright.
"""

# ========== Remote browser authentication ==========
# Hosted browsers may require an access token, passed as ?access_token=... in the CDP
# URL and sent as the X-Access-Token header. A local Chrome needs none of this.
# Global sandbox reference
_sandbox_instance = None

def connect_existing_sandbox(cdp_url, access_token):
    """Register the access token of a remote browser and set the global headers."""
    global _sandbox_instance, _cdp_headers
    _cdp_headers = {"X-Access-Token": access_token}
    print(f"✅ Using remote browser, CDP: {cdp_url[:60]}...")
    return cdp_url

# Internal headers cache
_cdp_headers = {}

def get_cdp_headers():
    """Get headers needed for CDP connection headers"""
    if _cdp_headers:
        return _cdp_headers
    if _sandbox_instance:
        return {"X-Access-Token": str(_sandbox_instance._envd_access_token)}
    return {}
# ========== End remote browser authentication ==========

browser_window_size_width = 1280
browser_window_size_height = 720

def extract_between_keywords(text, start_key, end_key):
    pattern = re.compile(f'{re.escape(start_key)}(.*?){re.escape(end_key)}', re.DOTALL)
    matches = pattern.findall(text)
    return [match.strip() for match in matches]

def extract_box_coordinate(response, box_name="start_box"):
    """Extract (x, y) coordinate from both formats:
    - New: start_box='<|box_start|>(x,y)<|box_end|>'
    - Old: start_box='(x,y)'
    """
    # New format with <|box_start|>...<|box_end|>
    m = re.search(rf"{box_name}='<\|box_start\|>\s*\(\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*(\d+)\s*\)\s*<\|box_end\|>'", response)
    if m:
        return int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    # Old format
    m = re.search(rf"{box_name}='\(\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*(\d+)\s*\)'", response)
    if m:
        return int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    return None

# Initialize Playwright
def init_playwright_context(url):
    p = sync_playwright().start()
    try:
        headers = get_cdp_headers()
        # Remote browser: take access_token from the URL's query string
        if not headers:
            parsed = urlparse(url)
            qs = parse_qs(parsed.query)
            token = qs.get('access_token', [None])[0]
            if token:
                connect_existing_sandbox(url, token)
                headers = get_cdp_headers()
                print(f"🔑 Found an access token in the CDP URL")
        browser = p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(url, **({"headers": headers} if headers else {}))
        # Get existing context or create new
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else browser.new_context()
    except Exception as e:
        print("init error", e)
        return None, None, None

    return p, browser, context

# Open webpage
def settle_after_navigation(page, floor_ms=None, ceil_ms=None):
    """Wait for the page to settle after navigation. Returns the milliseconds waited.

    **Replaces the old fixed `wait_for_timeout(3000)`**, which was a blind bet that
    3 seconds would do:

        page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded")   # DOM skeleton ready
        page.wait_for_timeout(3000)                     # then wait 3 s with eyes closed

    `domcontentloaded` only means the DOM tree exists, **not that the content is
    there**. Many target sites are SPAs and data portals whose pipeline is "DOM
    skeleton + spinner -> download and run the JS bundle -> data XHR -> render once
    the data arrives". On fast sites the 3 seconds are wasted; on slow ones they are
    not enough, so the step-0 screenshot shows a spinner and the model starts working
    on a page that has not formed yet. In one development set, 8 of 70 tasks kept
    complaining that the page had not loaded, and 6 of them ended without an answer.

    Three stages instead, **floor -> early exit -> ceiling**, and all three are needed:

      floor      covers pages that reach networkidle first and only draw content with
                 JS a moment later. Without it this change would wait *less* than the
                 old fixed 3 seconds; that is the only real risk in this function.
      early exit fast sites reach networkidle in about 0.7 s; no need to sit out 3 s.
      ceiling    pages with polling / analytics beacons / WebSockets *never* reach
                 "no connections for 500 ms"; without a cap we would wait until the
                 timeout. With it, the worst case is a fixed cost.

    Not settling is not an error: a `wait_for_load_state` timeout just means this
    page never goes quiet. Carry on and let the model judge from the screenshot (it
    still has wait() and reload()).
    """
    cfg = get_config()
    floor_ms = cfg.settle_floor_ms if floor_ms is None else floor_ms
    ceil_ms = cfg.settle_ceil_ms if ceil_ms is None else ceil_ms

    started = time.time()
    page.wait_for_timeout(floor_ms)
    for state in ("load", "networkidle"):
        remaining = ceil_ms - (time.time() - started) * 1000
        if remaining <= 0:
            break
        try:
            page.wait_for_load_state(state, timeout=remaining)
        except Exception:
            break          # this page never goes quiet (long-lived connections / polling / beacons); stop waiting
    return int((time.time() - started) * 1000)


def close_other_pages(context, keep):
    """Keep only the `keep` tab and close all others. Returns the number actually closed.

    A "single-tab reset" at the start of every task solves two problems:
      1. **capture.json contamination across tasks**: pages left over from the
         previous task keep sending requests in the background (polling, beacons,
         timed refreshes), and those would be recorded in this task's capture.json,
         where requests to another site make no sense. Unbinding listeners in
         RequestCollector.clear() is the first layer; closing the pages themselves is
         the second. A page that no longer exists leaves no trace at all.
      2. **State interference**: popups, login state or half-filled forms from the
         previous task sit in neighbouring tabs, and the model gets led astray if it
         switches to one.

    ⚠️ Create the new page before calling this. When a context drops to 0 pages, a
    CDP-connected browser is closed along with it, which is why the reference
    implementation kept one old page (`pages[:-1]`) rather than closing them all.
    Creating first and closing second removes that window, so everything can go.

    Failing to close a single page is not a failure: at worst one extra tab stays
    open, which must not bring down the whole task.
    """
    closed = 0
    for page in list(context.pages):
        if page is keep:
            continue
        try:
            try:
                page.evaluate("() => { window.stop(); }")  # stop in-flight requests first
            except Exception:
                pass
            page.close(run_before_unload=False)  # skip onbeforeunload confirmation dialogs
            closed += 1
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Failed to close leftover page: {e}")
    return closed


def open_page(p, browser, context, cdp_url, target_url, max_retries = 3):
    """Open the start page of a task: new tab (reconnecting CDP if the connection is
    broken) -> close other tabs -> size the viewport to the browser window -> add
    no-cache headers -> goto the start URL -> wait for first paint. Returns the new page.

    ⚠️ Called only at the start of a task (and for disconnect recovery when
    max_reconnect_per_task > 0; the shipped config sets 0). No model action can
    trigger it: "go back to the start page" is not in the action space.
    """
    # --- Fix code ---
    # Strip whitespace
    if target_url:
        target_url = target_url.strip()
    # Auto-complete https
    if target_url and not target_url.startswith("http"):
        target_url = "https://" + target_url
    # ----------------

    # print(f"🌐 Opening page: {target_url}", context)
    print(f"🌐 Opening page: {target_url}")
    page = None
    
    retry_count = 0
    while retry_count < max_retries:
        # Old pages are cleaned up only after the new page exists (close_other_pages
        # below). The order matters: at 0 pages, CDP takes the browser down too.
        try:
            # Try creating new page
            if context and len(context.pages) > 0:
                try:
                    page = context.new_page()
                    break
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"Failed to create page: {e}")
                    context = None
            
            # No context, or the page could not be created: reconnect
            if not context or not page:
                print(f"Reconnecting to browser... (attempt {retry_count + 1}/{max_retries})")
                
                # Try disconnecting existing connection first
                try:
                    if browser:
                        browser.close()
                except:
                    pass
                
                # Wait for connection to fully close
                import time
                time.sleep(2)
                
                # Reconnect
                try:
                    cdp_h = get_cdp_headers(); browser = p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(cdp_url, **({"headers": cdp_h} if cdp_h else {}))
                    # Wait for connection to stabilize
                    time.sleep(1)
                    
                    # Get or create context
                    if browser.contexts:
                        context = browser.contexts[0]
                    else:
                        context = browser.new_context()
                    
                    page = context.new_page()
                    break
                    
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"Connection failed: {e}")
                    retry_count += 1
                    if retry_count >= max_retries:
                        raise Exception(f"Cannot connect to browser after {max_retries}  times")
                    continue
                    
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error creating page: {e}")
            retry_count += 1
            if retry_count >= max_retries:
                raise

        raise Exception("Cannot create page")

    # Single-tab reset: the new page is ready, so closing the rest cannot drop the
    # page count to 0. It can be turned off with agent.single_tab_reset in config.json;
    # it is a kill switch, see the comment on RuntimeConfig.single_tab_reset.
    if get_config().single_tab_reset:
        n_closed = close_other_pages(page.context, keep=page)
        if n_closed:
            print(f"🧹 single-tab reset: closed {n_closed} leftover page(s)")
    else:
        print(f"⏭️ single-tab reset is off (single_tab_reset=false); {len(page.context.pages)} tab(s) open")

    # Set viewport size

        # Get browser window size

            () => {
                return {
                    availWidth: window.screen.availWidth,
                    availHeight: window.screen.availHeight,
                    width: window.outerWidth || 1920,
                    height: window.outerHeight || 1080
                }
            }
        """)
        
        print(f"Available screen size: {browser_window_size['availWidth']}x{browser_window_size['availHeight']}")
        print(f"Browser window size: {browser_window_size['width']}x{browser_window_size['height']}")
        
        global browser_window_size_width
        global browser_window_size_height
        
        browser_window_size_width = browser_window_size['width']
        browser_window_size_height = browser_window_size['height']

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Setting the viewport size failed: {e}; using the default")
        browser_window_size_width = 1920
        browser_window_size_height = 1080
        page.set_viewport_size({"width": 1920, "height": 1080})
    
    # Add no-cache headers to every request from the page
    def prevent_cache(route):

            headers['Cache-Control'] = 'no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate'
            headers['Pragma'] = 'no-cache'
            headers['Expires'] = '0'
            route.continue_(headers=headers)
        except:
            route.continue_()
    
    # Install the routing rule
    try:
        page.route('**/*', prevent_cache)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Failed to set the routing rule: {e}")
    
    # Navigate to the target URL
    try:
        page.goto(target_url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=150000)
        waited = settle_after_navigation(page)
        print(f"⏱️ first-paint settle {waited}ms")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Navigation failed: {e}")
        # Try a looser wait condition
        try:
            page.goto(target_url, wait_until="commit", timeout=60000)
        except:
            # Still failing: at least the page exists
            pass
    
    return page

# Save a screenshot
def save_screenshot(page, savePath, timeout_ms=5000, max_retries=3):
    """
    Save a screenshot, with retries.
    """
    # Make sure the directory exists (only needed once)
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(savePath), exist_ok=True)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"### failed to create directory: {str(e)}")
        return False

    for i in range(max_retries):
        try:
            # Take the screenshot
            page.screenshot(path=savePath, full_page=False, timeout=timeout_ms)
            print(f"### screenshot saved to: {savePath}")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"### screenshot failed (attempt {i+1}/{max_retries}): {str(e)}")
            if i < max_retries - 1:
                time.sleep(1)  # wait a moment before retrying
    
    return False

# CDP mouse move
def cdp_mouse_move(client, end_x, end_y, steps=20):
    """
    Emulate Playwright's multi-step page.mouse.move over the CDP protocol.
    
    params:
    client - CDP session
    end_x, end_y - target coordinates
    steps - number of intermediate moves
    """
    import time
    
    # Get the current mouse position first (assume a start position if that fails)
    try:
        # CDP has no direct way to read the mouse position, so ask JavaScript
        position = client.send("Runtime.evaluate", {
            "expression": "({x: window.mouseX || 0, y: window.mouseY || 0})",
            "returnByValue": True
        })
        start_x = position["result"]["value"]["x"]
        start_y = position["result"]["value"]["y"]
    except:
        # Unknown: assume the mouse starts at (0,0)
        start_x, start_y = 0, 0
    
    # Per-step increments
    delta_x = (end_x - start_x) / steps
    delta_y = (end_y - start_y) / steps
    
    # Move in steps
    for step in range(1, steps + 1):
        current_x = start_x + delta_x * step
        current_y = start_y + delta_y * step
        
        # Send the mouse-move event
        client.send("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", {
            "type": "mouseMoved", 
            "x": current_x, 
            "y": current_y
        })
        
        # Optional: a short delay makes the movement look more natural
        time.sleep(0.01)  # 10 ms
    
    # Remember the mouse position for the next call
    client.send("Runtime.evaluate", {
        "expression": f"window.mouseX = {end_x}; window.mouseY = {end_y};"
    })

# Click
def click(page, client, x, y, time_wait=500):

def doubleclick(page, client, x, y, time_wait=500):

    cdp_mouse_move(client, x, y, steps=20)
 
    time_wait = random.randint(time_wait // 2, time_wait)

# Hotkeys
# Browser-UI shortcuts: CDP's Input.dispatchKeyEvent only injects keys into the
# *page's renderer process* and cannot reach Chrome's own UI, so these keys are
# always no-ops, on every platform. Letting them fail silently is far more dangerous
# than rejecting them: the model gets no negative feedback and keeps retrying until
# the steps run out. In an early 10-task run, 100 of 335 actions were hotkeys, 87 of
# them of this kind, and 8 of the 10 tasks idled to the step limit with no answer.
BROWSER_LEVEL_HOTKEYS = {
    "ctrl+l", "alt+d", "meta+l",              # focus the address bar
    "f5", "ctrl+r", "meta+r", "ctrl+shift+r",  # reload
    "f6", "f11", "f12",                        # focus cycling / full screen / devtools
    "ctrl+shift+i", "ctrl+shift+j", "ctrl+shift+c", "meta+alt+i", "meta+alt+j",
    "ctrl+t", "meta+t", "ctrl+w", "meta+w", "ctrl+shift+t",  # tab management
    "ctrl+n", "meta+n", "ctrl+shift+n",
    "ctrl+tab", "ctrl+shift+tab",
    "alt+left", "alt+right", "meta+left", "meta+right",       # history back / forward
    "ctrl+d", "meta+d", "ctrl+h", "ctrl+j", "ctrl+shift+delete",
}


class UnsupportedHotkey(Exception):
    """The model asked for a shortcut that CDP cannot deliver to the browser UI."""


def hotkey(page, client, hot_key_value, time_wait=500):
    """Press a hotkey. Browser-level shortcuts (see BROWSER_LEVEL_HOTKEYS) raise
    UnsupportedHotkey here and the executor passes the reason to the model. Single keys
    go out as CDP key events, combinations through Playwright's keyboard.press.
    """
    # Map common key names to Playwright's names
    key_map = {
        "ctrl": "Control", "control": "Control",
        "alt": "Alt", "shift": "Shift",
        "meta": "Meta", "cmd": "Meta", "command": "Meta",
        "enter": "Enter", "return": "Enter",
        "tab": "Tab", "escape": "Escape", "esc": "Escape",
        "backspace": "Backspace", "delete": "Delete", "del": "Delete",
        "space": " ", "arrowup": "ArrowUp", "arrowdown": "ArrowDown",
        "arrowleft": "ArrowLeft", "arrowright": "ArrowRight",
        # The model often writes bare arrow names ("alt+Down"); without these Playwright raises "Unknown key"
        "up": "ArrowUp", "down": "ArrowDown",
        "left": "ArrowLeft", "right": "ArrowRight",
        "home": "Home", "end": "End",
        "pageup": "PageUp", "pagedown": "PageDown",
        "pgup": "PageUp", "pgdn": "PageDown", "pgdown": "PageDown",
    }

    # Normalize, then check the block-list (order- and case-insensitive)
    _parts = [k.strip().lower() for k in (
        hot_key_value.split("+") if "+" in hot_key_value else hot_key_value.strip().split())]
    _norm = "+".join(_parts)
    _norm_sorted = "+".join(sorted(_parts))
    if _norm in BROWSER_LEVEL_HOTKEYS or _norm_sorted in {
            "+".join(sorted(k.split("+"))) for k in BROWSER_LEVEL_HOTKEYS}:
        raise UnsupportedHotkey(
            f"hotkey(key='{hot_key_value}') is a browser-UI shortcut and cannot be delivered "
            f"to the page. It did NOT run. There is no way to navigate by URL. "
            f"If you wanted to refresh the page, use reload(). Do not retry this key.")

    # CDP keyCodes (for CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent)
    cdp_key_codes = {
        "Enter": 13, "Tab": 9, "Escape": 27, "Backspace": 8, "Delete": 46,
        " ": 32, "ArrowUp": 38, "ArrowDown": 40, "ArrowLeft": 37, "ArrowRight": 39,
        "Home": 36, "End": 35, "PageUp": 33, "PageDown": 34,
    }

    # Accepts "ctrl+a", "ctrl+shift+t", "ctrl a", "enter", ...
    if "+" in hot_key_value:
        keys = [k.strip() for k in hot_key_value.split("+")]
    else:
        keys = hot_key_value.strip().split()
    mapped = [key_map.get(k.lower(), k) for k in keys]

    # A single key with a CDP keyCode: send it directly over CDP (more reliable)
    if len(mapped) == 1 and mapped[0] in cdp_key_codes:
        key_name = mapped[0]
        key_code = cdp_key_codes[key_name]
        client.send("Input.dispatchKeyEvent", {
            "type": "keyDown",
            "windowsVirtualKeyCode": key_code,
            "code": key_name,
            "key": key_name,
        })
        client.send("Input.dispatchKeyEvent", {
            "type": "keyUp",
            "windowsVirtualKeyCode": key_code,
            "code": key_name,
            "key": key_name,
        })
    else:
        # Combinations go through Playwright's keyboard.press
        combo = "+".join(mapped)
        page.keyboard.press(combo)

    page.wait_for_timeout(time_wait)
    return page, client

# Typing
def click_type(page, client, x, y, content, time_wait=500):
    """Execute type(): optionally click the coordinates first (current callers pass -1 =
    no click), then select all, delete, and type character by character.
    Keys go to **whatever has focus**, which the previous click decided; to target an
    input box reliably, use fill().
    """
    # 1. Click via CDP
    if x != -1 and y != -1:
        page, client = click(page, client, x, y, time_wait) 
        page.wait_for_timeout(random.randint(100, 200))
    
    system = platform.system()
    
    if system == "Darwin":  # macOS
        # Command+A (Meta+A) on macOS
        page.keyboard.press("Meta+a")
    else:  # Windows and Linux
        # Control+A on Windows and Linux
        page.keyboard.press("Control+a")
    page.keyboard.press('Backspace')
    page.wait_for_timeout(2500)

    for char in content:
        page.keyboard.type(char, delay=random.randint(10, 50))

    # Pause 2 s afterwards
    page.wait_for_timeout(2000)

    return page, client

# Scroll
def scroll(page, client, delta_x, delta_y):
    viewport_size = page.viewport_size
    center_x = viewport_size["width"] / 2
    center_y = viewport_size["height"] / 2
    client.send("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", {
        "type": "mouseWheel",
        "x": center_x,
        "y": center_y,
        "deltaX": delta_x, # positive scrolls down, negative scrolls up
        "deltaY": delta_y  # positive scrolls down, negative scrolls up
    })
    return page, client

# Scroll at a given point (e.g. inside a menu)
def scroll_menu(page, client, x, y, delta_x, delta_y):
    print("x,y,delta_y:", x, y, delta_y)
    cdp_mouse_move(client, x, y, steps=20)
    client.send("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", {
        "type": "mouseWheel",
        "x": x,
        "y": y,
        "deltaX": delta_x,
        "deltaY": delta_y  # positive scrolls down, negative scrolls up
    })
    return page, client

# Drag
def drag(page, client, x1, y1, x2, y2, steps=20):
    """
    page - Playwright page
    client - CDP session
    x1, y1 - start coordinates
    x2, y2 - target coordinates
    steps - number of intermediate moves
    """
    import time
    
    # 1. Move the mouse to the start position
    cdp_mouse_move(client, x1, y1, steps=steps)
    page.wait_for_timeout(100)
    
    # 2. Press the left button
    client.send("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", {
        "type": "mousePressed",
        "x": x1,
        "y": y1,
        "button": "left",
        "clickCount": 1
    })
    page.wait_for_timeout(100)
    
    # 3. Move to the target in steps
    delta_x = (x2 - x1) / steps
    delta_y = (y2 - y1) / steps
    
    for step in range(1, steps + 1):
        current_x = x1 + delta_x * step
        current_y = y1 + delta_y * step
        
        client.send("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", {
            "type": "mouseMoved",
            "x": current_x,
            "y": current_y,
            "button": "left",  # keep the button down while dragging
            "buttons": 1       # left button pressed
        })
        
        # A short delay makes the drag look more natural
        time.sleep(0.01)  # 10 ms
    
    # 4. Release at the target
    client.send("Input.dispatchMouseEvent", {
        "type": "mouseReleased",
        "x": x2,
        "y": y2,
        "button": "left",
        "clickCount": 1
    })
    
    page.wait_for_timeout(2000)  # let the drag take effect
    return page, client

# Wait
def wait(page, client, time):
    page.wait_for_timeout(time)
    return page, client

# Step accounting
def step_cost(action):
    """How many steps this action counts as. A compound action counts once per browser
    operation: a click_many that clicks 4 squares is 4 steps. The max_steps budget is
    charged the same way; otherwise 6 rounds of 16 points would look like 6 steps
    while the browser was operated 96 times. Every other action is 1."""
    if action.get("name") == "ClickMany":
        return max(1, min(len(action.get("points") or []), MAX_CLICK_MANY_POINTS))
    return 1


def parse_action_type(action_str):
    """Action type from the start of the action string. agent.predict() uses it to detect the end (Finish / Wait / CallUser)."""
    action_str = action_str.strip()
    if action_str.startswith('click_many('):
        return 'ClickMany'
    if action_str.startswith('click('):
        return 'LeftClick'
    elif action_str.startswith('doubleclick(') or action_str.startswith('left_double('):
        return 'DoubleClick'
    elif action_str.startswith('right_single('):
        return 'RightClick'
    elif action_str.startswith('hover('):
        return 'Hover'
    elif action_str.startswith('select('):
        return 'Select'
    elif action_str.startswith('drag('):
        return 'Drag'
    elif action_str.startswith('hotkey(') or action_str.startswith('hotkey '):
        return 'Hotkey'
    elif action_str.startswith('reload('):
        return 'Reload'
    elif action_str.startswith('back('):
        return 'Back'
    elif action_str.startswith('find_text('):
        return 'FindText'
    elif action_str.startswith('read_text('):
        return 'ReadText'
    elif action_str.startswith('fill('):
        return 'Fill'
    elif action_str.startswith('type('):
        return 'Type'
    elif action_str.startswith('stop('):
        return 'Stop'
    elif action_str.startswith('scroll'):
        # current action-space format
        if "scroll(" in action_str: 
            if "up" in action_str:
                return 'ScrollUp'
            elif "down" in action_str:
                return 'ScrollDown'
            elif "left" in action_str:
                return 'ScrollLeft'
            elif "right" in action_str:
                return 'ScrollRight'
            else:
                print("scroll parse error !")
                exit()
        else:
            print("scroll parse error !")
            exit()
    elif action_str.startswith('goto('):
        return 'Goto'
    elif action_str.startswith('finished(') or action_str.startswith('finish('):
        return 'Finish'
    elif action_str == 'wait()':
        return 'Wait'
    elif action_str == 'call_user()':
        return 'CallUser'
    else:
        return 'Unknown'
           
# Parse an action
def parse_action(action_str):
    """Parse the model's action string into the executor's dict: {"name": ..., "coordinate" / "value" / ...}.

    excute_action() dispatches only on the name returned here. A new action needs a
